- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in recognizing momentum; shift forecast upward by 1–3% per day for 3–5 days following sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if model consistently forecasts above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven periods; add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after spike, model often fails to anticipate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days if sentiment turns negative after spike.
